items.name: Readability
items.evidence: `compile_json_key` adds an Oracle-only `key.replace("%", "%%")` branch with no comment explaining why. It also takes `compiler` but never uses it. One line breaks the black line limit: `return "(NOT %s OR %s IS NULL)" % (sql, lhs), tuple(lhs_params) + tuple(lhs_params)`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The `JSON_EXISTS(%s, '%s')` / `compile_json_path(lhs_key_transforms)` SQL is copied into both KeyTransformIsNull.as_oracle and KeyTransformExact.as_oracle. A small HasKey subclass would have avoided this, as the conventions ask. The `get_prep_lookup` changes to HasKey and HasKeys go beyond the fix. The unused `compiler` parameter remains.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No errors are swallowed. The Oracle `%` escaping is special-cased ad hoc in one place only. The inlined Oracle JSON_EXISTS paths drop that escaping. `json.dumps(str(key))` silently converts any non-str key, with no validation.

items.name: Array-index semantics kept for isnull / exact=None paths
items.name_zh: isnull / exact=None 路径保留数组下标语义
items.evidence: The final key goes through `self.compile_json_key` -> `".%s" % json.dumps(str(key))` in the shared HasKeyLookup.as_sql, used by SQLite, MySQL and Oracle. Leading segments still use compile_json_path. The isnull (SQLite/Oracle) and Oracle exact=None paths now use compile_json_path directly, so array indices still work. This is done by inlining rather than a subclass.
